title: Privacy-Preserved Neural Graph Databases

problem.claim: Neural graph databases can infer hidden relationships and answer queries over incomplete graphs, but their generalization ability creates privacy risks for domain-specific or private databases.

gap.claim: Existing neural graph database capabilities can allow attackers to infer sensitive information through combinations of seemingly innocuous queries, including information removed during training.

contributions.claim: A privacy-preserved neural graph database framework, called P-NGDB, is proposed to alleviate privacy leakage risks in neural graph databases.
Adversarial training is introduced to make answers generated for queries involving private information indistinguishable and increase resistance to inference from combinations of multiple queries.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on three datasets.
The authors report that the framework protects private information while maintaining high-quality public query answers.
The authors report that the code is available in a public repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Efficient and accurate retrieval is important for using domain-specific or private data with retrieval-augmented generation.
Neural graph databases combine graph databases and neural networks, using neural embeddings and complex neural logical query answering to support storage, retrieval, analysis, and generalization.
The ability to infer latent graph structure and answer queries introduces privacy risks, including sensitive information inference through query combinations.
P-NGDB addresses the risk with adversarial training intended to produce indistinguishable answers for private information queries.
Experiments on three datasets are reported to show privacy protection and high-quality public query responses; code availability is also reported.

source_observation.claim: Improved inference over incomplete graph data can expose sensitive information even when that information was removed during training.

interpretation.claim: Privacy evaluation should consider inference enabled by combinations of outputs, not only direct memorization or explicit disclosure.

application.claim: For systems that answer queries over private or domain-specific graph data, evaluate whether multiple innocuous queries can be combined to recover sensitive attributes.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how broadly this threat model applies beyond the described neural graph database setting.

source_observation.claim: Adversarial training is used to make answers involving private information indistinguishable.

interpretation.claim: Training objectives can be designed to reduce the distinguishability of privacy-sensitive outputs while preserving utility.

application.claim: Consider adversarial training when a query-answering system must limit privacy leakage without eliminating public-answer functionality.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the privacy guarantees, attack assumptions, or utility trade-offs achieved by the training method.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or experimental results.
The abstract does not define the privacy threat model or formal privacy guarantees.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture or adversarial training procedure.
The abstract does not report limitations, failure cases, or computational costs.
